page: Vultr vbm-8c-64gb-amd is a bare metal server configured with an AMD EPYC 4345P processor operating at 3.9 GHz. This x86_64 architecture system features 8 physical cores and 2 threads per core, providing 16 dedicated vCPUs. The hardware includes 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and is equipped with 3890 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. No GPU accelerators are present on this server.

Benchmark results show top-tier performance in single-core operations, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all ranking in the top 10%. Passmark memory score also falls into the top 10%. Conversely, multi-core CPU performance, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Passmark CPU scores are in the average range. Large block memory write bandwidth is a relative bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 25%, while read-only memory bandwidth remains average.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this bare metal server offers high local storage density and strong single-core performance relative to its resource footprint. The primary tradeoff is the lower multi-core scaling and weak large-block memory write speeds compared to higher-end multi-socket systems. This hardware profile is suited for workloads requiring high single-threaded processing speeds, substantial local NVMe storage, and moderate memory capacity, such as database hosting, static web serving, and lightweight LLM inference tasks.
